relationship: Grouping departments into local networks connects subnet design to the broadcast and routing consequences in two scenarios.

learnerLoop.action: Play the network story, edit department groups and apply a subnet design.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The draft and applied subnet arrangement change.
learnerLoop.evidence: Story steps, metrics and the network view show the design's effects.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Move a department or compare the before-subnetting and designed-network outcomes.

invariants: Applied metrics reflect the selected scenario and subnet arrangement.
The learner can return from the draft grouping to revise it.
safeAdaptations: Change organisation stories, department names or guidance while preserving editable grouping and consequence comparison.
nonGoals: Replacing an IP address-planning or router configuration tool.

task.description: Compare a flat broadcast domain with a learner-grouped subnet design.
task.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

model.description: Department nodes, broadcast boundaries, routing and optional IP packet decisions.
model.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

planner.description: Gated placement of departments into subnet groups and optional address allocations.
planner.visibility: Locked until a baseline traffic story completes; builder is generated from draft groups.

evidence.description: Current packet decision, interrupted device counts, router forwarding and boundary explanation.
evidence.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

departments.description: Device demand assigned to subnet groups.
departments.domain: Admin 10, Classrooms 28, Media 12, IoT 18 and Servers 4.
departments.source: Fixed department model plus learner placements.

allocation.description: Address blocks for the selected groups.
allocation.domain: Two to four nonempty groups; smallest fitting CIDR blocks, including gateway demand.
allocation.output: Optional address details and router interface reads.

traffic.description: Devices interrupted and router forwards during a story.
traffic.domain: Whole-number counts accumulated across the selected path.
traffic.source: Noisy sensor or server request story.

modes.view: Before subnetting and Your design; the design is gated by baseline completion.
modes.story: Noisy sensor or Find the server. Next/Play slowly share the same steps.
modes.ip: Optional IP walkthrough reveals mask/AND, local-versus-gateway and frame decisions.
modes.support: No None/Some/All or exam mapping toggle.

dependencies: Finish either baseline story to unlock planning.
All five departments must be assigned to two to four nonempty groups before applying.
The applied layout determines subsequent broadcast and routed request evidence.
implementation.completion: Each traffic story finishes at its last decision; learners can revise an applied design and rerun the comparison.
limitations: Fixed campus demands and simplified teaching traffic.
Address/IP details are optional views, not qualification mappings.
